source.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Curriculum Induction
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2020

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed (NeurIPS 2020) method paper demonstrating that an automatic instructor/teacher providing an adaptive intervention curriculum (a library of reset controllers, activated when the agent behaves dangerously) lets an RL agent learn a hazardous task safely and successfully where unscaffolded learning fails. This is the ML-side grounding for the scaffolded_sd054_onboarding curriculum design: it shows hazard-avoidance is learnable as a staged, externally-scaffolded competency. Confidence 0.62 (lowest in the review by design): it is a methods analogue informing curriculum engineering, not biological evidence for a REE claim, and the biology-before-formal-definitions principle means it must not by itself drive a substrate mechanism decision.
failure_signatures: If hazardous tasks were learnable by direct, unscaffolded RL, the curriculum-induction machinery would be unnecessary -- the paper's premise is that the agent must 'behave safely not only after but also while learning', which fails without an instructor; this is the ML mirror of the 603g isolated-stage failure.

The teacher here is an EXTERNAL monitor with reset controllers, analogous to the maternal-buffering scaffold in the developmental biology; if REE expects the agent to self-bootstrap avoidance with no external scaffold or protective regime, this paper predicts it will not learn safely within budget.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In safety-critical settings an agent must behave safely while learning, not only after. Prior safe-RL relies on priors/smoothness assumptions that often fail. Instead, an automatic instructor (a monitor with a library of reset controllers that it activates when the agent starts behaving dangerously) prevents harm during exploration; the teacher learns, from observing the agent's progress, a policy over which reset controller to apply when -- a curriculum -- that optimises the agent's final policy reward. Demonstrated to induce curricula for safe and efficient learning in two environments.
mapping.ree_translation: Maps to the scaffolded_sd054_onboarding curriculum design (SD-054 family): hazard-avoidance is learnable when an external scaffold intervenes during acquisition and is gradually withdrawn, rather than expecting the agent to learn survival in one unscaffolded isolated stage (the 603g Stage-H shape). The reset-controller/instructor is the ML analogue of the maternal-buffering scaffold in the developmental biology entries -- both supply protection-during-acquisition. Supports redesigning the onboarding as a staged, teacher/reset-scaffolded avoidance curriculum, with the protective intervention annealed as competence grows.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a METHODS analogue, not biological evidence and not evidence for any REE assertion-claim. Per the project's biology-before-formal-definitions principle it must not, on its own, drive a substrate mechanism choice; its role is to show the curriculum shape is feasible and to constrain the engineering, while the SD-035/MECH-279 biology entries carry the mechanism question. The paper's environments (e.g. driving-like, gridworld) are not REE's foraging-under-hazard substrate, and the reset-controller abstraction may not have a clean REE homologue.
mapping.source_context: Computational RL experiments in two simulated safety-critical environments; teacher-student (instructor + reset-controller) framework, NeurIPS 2020.

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue (NeurIPS 2020). Mapping fidelity deliberately moderate -- it informs curriculum engineering, not substrate mechanism. Transfer risk elevated: ML method to REE substrate, and it is parallel/methodological evidence (lit signal), decoupled from experimental confidence per the lit/exp decoupling policy.
